newsitem.title: USA: Mobil, Shell to combine Calififornia production.
newsitem.headline: Mobil, Shell to combine Calififornia production.

text.p: Mobil Corp. said Wednesday it agreed with Shell Oil Co. to form a new company consisting of the California oil producing operations of both companies.

The company would be the largest oil producer in the state, with combined proven reserves equivalent to more than 1 billion barrels of oil and production of approximately 250,000 barrels per day, Mobil said.

It said the deal was the result of talks between Mobil's domestic exploration and production business unit, Mobil Exploration & Producing U.S. Inc., and CalResources LLC, an affiliate of Shell Oil, which is itself a unit of Royal Dutch Shell.
Mobil said it would own a 40 percent equity interest in the new company, with CalResources holding the remaining 60 percent interest.
Mobil and CalResources currently produce about 100,000 barrels daily and 150,000 barrels daily, respectively, in California.
Final agreement on the new alliance will be contingent on reaching definitive agreements, regulatory approvals, and approval by directors of both parent companies.

"The proximity of Mobil and CalResources operations in two of California's largest heavy oil fields provides the opportunity to reduce expenses and capital costs, eliminate duplication and achieve economies of scale that the two companies could not achieve continuing to operate on a stand-alone basis," said Mike Yeager, president and general manager of Mobil Exploration US.
The new company, which is expected to start operations by mid-1997, would be based in Bakersfield, Calif., where Mobil and CalResources currently employ 500 and 875 people, respectively.
Mobil said its California-based refining, retail petroleum products marketing and pipeline operations are not part of the proposed new business and are not expected to be affected by the new company.
